subject: Product roadmap exception: Lagoon Health accelerated feature request
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: 2026-08-30 09:12 -0700
Subject: Product roadmap exception: Lagoon Health accelerated feature request

Team —

Quick background: Lagoon Health (commercial payer) is asking us to ship two small but high-impact items before their production go-live on 2026-10-15. They’ve put a 12-month committed seat contract on the table contingent on these features being in our supported stack by that date. High level ask:

1) Per-tenant cache warmup + soft reservation so customer can pre-seed KV/prefix for predictable cold-start latency on morning batches.
2) 24-hour export of audit logs and request traces in a simplified CSV schema for downstream compliance ingestion.

I’ve attached their latest SOW (Lagoon_SOW_v3.pdf) and their completed security questionnaire. Procurement (ProcureCorp) also sent a note that they can fast-track signatures if we can give a clear delivery window.

Immediate asks for this thread:
- Product/Eng: feasibility + rough ETA and risk (Karthik/Jasmine)
- CS: proposed mitigation plan if full implementation slips (Marissa)
- Sales: confirm customer commitment (me)

Customer is prepared to convert to dedicated/reserved capacity and accept a paid pilot with standing SLA. This looks like a substantial expansion if we can deliver.

Thanks —
Ben
Ben Carter | Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
Attachments: Lagoon_SOW_v3.pdf, Lagoon_security_qs_filled.xlsx

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-30 11:03 -0700
Subject: Re: Product roadmap exception: Lagoon Health accelerated feature request

Thanks for the context, Ben.

A few quick clarifying points before we loop in the broader Eng team:
- Are they asking for a built-in runtime feature (first-class API) or would a documented deployment pattern + runbook suffice for the first release?
- Does "24-hour export" mean push to customer S3 or a downloadable CSV via Console?

Karthik/Jasmine — please call out: required infra changes, expected engineering effort (sprint estimate), whether a canary approach is practical (i.e., implement for Lagoon only for first 8 weeks). If we can ship a narrow MVP that hits their acceptance criteria, we can buy time to generalize.

I’ll confirm commercial terms with Anita/Tom and ask them to sign the SOW on expedited timeline if we can give a delivery window. Ben — can you confirm procurement contact?

Also tagging the HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.com/deals/LHN-2026-03

—Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni | Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-31 08:40 -0700
Subject: Re: Product roadmap exception: Lagoon Health accelerated feature request

On Mon, Aug 30, 2026 at 11:03 AM Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com> wrote:
> A few quick clarifying points before we loop in the broader Eng team:
> - Are they asking for a built-in runtime feature (first-class API) or would a documented deployment pattern + runbook suffice for the first release?
> - Does "24-hour export" mean push to customer S3 or a downloadable CSV via Console?

Thanks — good questions. Short answer: we can likely deliver a scoped, tenant-level "warmup" shim and a scheduled export job as a thin feature without touching the core attention/runtime kernels, but there are trade-offs:

- Warmup approach options (pros/cons):
  * Prefill KV cache on startup using a pre-seeded prefix (low complexity, bounded memory cost) — estimate 2 engineer-weeks plus QA and infra changes to allow per-tenant scheduling.
  * Reservation tokens tied to dedicated pools (more invasive) — estimate 4-6 engineer-weeks and SLA implications.

- Export: pushing to customer S3 with a small CSV serializer is trivial (~3 engineer-days) if we reuse existing trace export plumbing; adding a Console UI download is another 1-2 sprints.

Given the timeline (need shipped by 2026-10-15 to hit procurement), we can do an MVP of prefilling + S3 export if customer accepts a one-tenant canary and explicit documented limitations.

Risks: prioritization will displace current sprint items (ENG-1227 backlog). We need formal approval from Product leadership to re-prioritize. Also need the SOW signed to justify dedicating cycles.

Actionable from Eng:
- Jasmine: please sanity-check the 2-week estimate for the prefilling shim and call out ops changes.
- If approved, I propose we create a focused ticket (ENG-1227) and push a 2-sprint hotfix lane.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer | VP, Product Engineering

From: Anita Shah <anita.shah@lagoonhealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Hsu <tom.hsu@lagoonhealth.com>, sourcing@procurecorp.com
Date: 2026-09-01 09:22 -0700
Subject: Re: Product roadmap exception: Lagoon Health accelerated feature request

Hi all —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. To be explicit on our side:
- We need deterministic morning latency (6–10am ET batch window) for claims enrichment.
- Export to our S3 bucket is acceptable. We need the first automated daily export by 2026-10-12 to begin validation with our downstream systems.
- We will commit to a 12‑month reserved capacity contract and sign the attached SOW (Lagoon_SOW_v3.pdf) within 48 hours if you provide a reasonable delivery plan.

Procurement: ProcureCorp can issue PO within 5 business days of SOW signature. Their main ask is a clear delivery milestone and rollback plan if the feature impacts production SLAs.

Happy to hop on a quick call tomorrow to align.

—Anita Shah
Head of Platform Integrations | Lagoon Health
Attachments: Lagoon_SOW_v3.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-01 14:05 -0700
Subject: Re: Product roadmap exception: Lagoon Health accelerated feature request

Thanks Anita — appreciate the clarity. From CS/implementation POV, here's a minimal acceptance plan we can propose to Lagoon:

1) Pilot (Lagoon-only): enable prefilling shim + S3 export on a dedicated reserved pool. Run for 4 weeks.
2) Performance gates: 99th p50/p95 targets during the 6–10am window. If gates fail, we fall back to soft-throttling + retry policy (runbook included).
3) Rollout: after successful 4-week pilot, productize across other reserved customers in Q4.

I'll attach an annotated scope sketch (MVP_scope_sketch.png) with proposed validation criteria. If Engineering can confirm the 2-week development estimate for the shim and the 3 day export, we can propose an internal timeline that meets Anita's 10/12 target (engineering work completed by 09/30; QA and canary in early October).

Marissa Cole | Customer Success Director, Strategic Accounts
Attachments: MVP_scope_sketch.png

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Product roadmap exception: Lagoon Health accelerated feature request

All — we have a commercial commitment on the table (12-mo reserved + expedited PO) if we can provide a delivery plan. Decision: I’m requesting we open a Product exception and place ENG-1227 on the "priority lane" for the next two sprints, scoped as Karthik suggested (prefill shim + S3 export as MVP).

Action items assigned:
- Karthik/Jasmine: create ENG-1227, include spike tasks, and post initial ETA by EOD 2026-09-03. Please note this will require resource reallocation; include which planned items will slip.
- Marissa: finalize the pilot validation criteria document and SRE rollback runbook. Attachments to suggest: MVP_scope_sketch.png (done) + Lagoon_SOW_v3.pdf.
- Ben: confirm procurement contact and get signed SOW scanned to sourcing@procurecorp.com within 48 hours.

If Product leadership pushes back on priority, escalate to execs — this is a near-term revenue motion and a multi-quarter footprint expansion. I’ll follow up with a short summary to the Exec channel if we need the formal sign-off.

Thanks —
Vivek Kulkarni | Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
